headline: Lead AI Product Designer
positioning: I design AI products and the design systems behind them, so that what a model produces is something a person can check, trust and act on.
summary: I'm Mohammad Abdul Aleem, a Lead AI Product Designer in Hyderabad. Thirteen-plus years in enterprise UX taught me that trust is a design outcome: it comes from clear states, honest copy, accessible components and systems that behave the same way every time.

Today I spend most of my time on design systems that engineers and AI agents can both build from, and on the product flows where a model’s output meets a person who has to act on it. More and more, the first user of those flows is an agent acting for a person, so I design for both, and for the handoff between them.

Where I am heading: product and AI leadership, owning the roadmap, the priorities and the outcomes as well as the screens. My design, enterprise and fintech work is the foundation for it, not something I leave behind.

principles.title: Trust is designed, not declared
principles.body: Every AI state gets a deliberate design: thinking, unsure, wrong and recovering. A confident UI over an uncertain model is a lie users eventually catch.

principles.title: Ship the system, not the screen
principles.body: Tokens, components and spec files outlive any single mock-up. If an engineer or an agent can't rebuild it from the spec, it isn't done.

principles.title: Accessible by default
principles.body: WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor, checked in code, not a final-week audit. It also makes AI output usable by more people.

career.summary: Design across product, marketing, AI research and AI agent teams: enterprise products, web experiences, multi-brand design systems and AI-assisted workflows.
highlights: Cut text below WCAG AA contrast on an AI freight platform’s console from 1,646 nodes to 7 in light mode across 97 screens in testing, by re-theming it on its own design system and building an audit skill that checks every screen in both themes.
Made five brands’ colours accessible, with all 80 measured colour pairs meeting WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark, by building every brand on one component library.

Gave developers, coding agents and the sales and marketing team one source for on-brand work, built out to 20 typed React components, 15 templates and 231 token values, by creating and maintaining the Colaberry Design System.
Made IT access requests ready for an ISO 27001 audit, with 10 of 14 IT action items completed, by generating the access log from Basecamp instead of typing it into Excel.
Redesigned the AI Systems Architect Accelerator homepage and three audience landing pages, by designing them in Claude Design and leading QA across the site.
Brought gamification, presence and chat to the learner portal, all three now in production, by designing the features.
Set design direction for AI-assisted development and the UX team, by writing UI prompt packs and design playbooks, mentoring the team and designing AgentCory’s UX flows and explainers.

career.summary: Became Senior Product Designer on the Latitude account and modernised its legacy enterprise interfaces, with accessibility as part of the brief.
highlights: Brought the Latitude account’s legacy enterprise interfaces to WCAG conformance, by modernising them with accessibility as part of the brief.
Grounded design decisions in what users actually did, by running user research and usability testing.
Aligned stakeholders on the problem before the solution, by leading design workshops.
Gave stakeholders their metrics in real time, by designing live metric dashboards.

career.summary: A short assignment on the same Latitude account: worked directly with the Product Owner, handled the tickets, and wrote the business requirements document and the user stories in Jira for the client.
highlights: Defined how customer letters would be automated, by analysing the customer-letter processes and writing their requirements.
Gave the team one picture of every letter type, by delivering flow maps, personas and solution documentation for each.

career.summary: Joined NTT DATA India as a designer in a small agile web team for its client Latitude Financial Services, Australia, working in quarterly sprints.
highlights: Kept new screens consistent with the client’s brand, by producing high-fidelity designs inside its design system and design language.
Redesigned the client’s mobile app interfaces and web pages.
Shaped page layouts around search requirements, by working with the digital marketing team.

career.summary: Led the design of a fintech platform.
highlights: Let new fintech work start from shared parts, by building reusable design frameworks.
Refined the platform’s interface on evidence, by running A/B tests and reading behaviour analytics in Google Analytics and Hotjar.

career.summary: Designed responsive healthcare web applications with agile development teams.
Designed websites where search visibility and usability were joint requirements.

expertise.title: AI product design
expertise.body: Flows where a model’s output meets a person who has to act on it: states for thinking, unsure and wrong, review steps, honest copy, and the handoff back to the person when an agent has done the work.

expertise.title: Enterprise UX
expertise.body: Dashboards, workflows and data-heavy internal tools, where clarity under load is the job.

expertise.title: Design systems
expertise.body: Tokens, accessible components and spec files that engineers and coding agents can both build from.

expertise.title: Research and UX strategy
expertise.body: User research, usability testing, process mapping and stakeholder workshops that settle the problem before the solution.

expertise.title: Interaction design and prototyping
expertise.body: From flows to high-fidelity prototypes and implementation guidance for the team that builds it.

expertise.title: Design leadership
expertise.body: Mentoring designers, running design QA and working across product, marketing, sales and engineering.

aiWorkflow.title: Understand the workflow
aiWorkflow.body: I start with the business problem and how the work is done today, before any screen.

aiWorkflow.title: Redesign it
aiWorkflow.body: I redraw the workflow around the person who has to act, and decide where a model helps and where a person must check.

aiWorkflow.title: Build it with AI
aiWorkflow.body: I use Claude and other generative tools every day for UI exploration, interaction design, documentation and reusable prompts, working from a design system so the output stays on-system.

aiWorkflow.title: Validate it with people
aiWorkflow.body: I prototype, test with users and stay with the work through design-to-development handoff until it is in production.

aiWorkflow.title: Design for both users
aiWorkflow.body: Where an agent acts for the person, I check that it can read and finish the task, that the moment control returns to the person is designed, and that the agent is helped to serve the person rather than steered to serve us.
